title: תפילה ליום הכיפורים | Prayer for Yom Kippur by Rabbi Dr. Aryeh Cohen
author: Aryeh Cohen

coauthors.name: Aryeh Cohen
coauthors.bio: Aryeh Cohen is a professor, a social justice activist, a rabbi, and a lecturer. He teaches all things Rabbinic Literature (Mishnah, Talmud, midrash) and social justice at the Ziegler School for Rabbinic Studies of the American Jewish University. Prof. Cohen is a founder and member of the Shtibl Minyan, a former chair of the Boards of the Progressive Jewish Alliance, and CLUE. He is the co-convener of the Black Jewish Justice Alliance and is the author of Justice in the City: An Argument from the Sources of Rabbinic Judaism (2012).

content:
This is a prayer for Yom Kippur. It started out as a meditation on Yizkor, hence the אל מלא רחמים form at the beginning. It quickly changed to a prayer for insight and change and the possiblity of tshuvah in this moment.
Source (Hebrew) Translation (English)
‏אֵל מְלֵאַת רַחֲמִים, שׁוֹכֶנֶת בַּמְּרוֹמִים
אֲשֶׁר בָּרָאת עוֹלָם וּמְלוֹאוֹ יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן
הַמְצִיאִי בְּנוֹ
רַחֲמִים מֵעֵבֶר לַכְּאֵב
‏אֶמְפַּתְיָה מֵעֵבֶר לַפַּחַד
‏הַכָּרָה מֵעֵבֶר לַאֲטִימוּת
God full of mercy, who dwells on high
who has created the world and all that is in it out of nothing
engineer in us
mercy beyond the pain
empathy beyond the fear
recognition beyond the obtuseness
אָנָּא ה׳ הַשְׁכִּינִי בְּתוֹכֵנוּ
כֹּחַ לְהִתְאַבֵּל עַל הָאַחֵר
כֹּשֶׁר לְהִסְתַּכֵּל עַל הַהֶרֶס
אֹמֶץ לִבְכּוֹת אֶת הָאָדָם בַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא/הִיא אָדָם
Please O God, make dwell in us
power to grieve for the other
ability to look upon the destruction
strength to cry for the human because they are human
הַפַּח נִשְׁבָּר וַאֲנַחְנוּ נִמְלָטְנוּ
הַהֲזָיָה נִשְׁבְּרָה וְהַפַּח הוּא אֲנַחְנוּ
יָדֵינוּ דָּמִים מָלְאוּ וְלֹא דָמֵינוּ
אֵם הָרַחֲמִים וְהַסְּלִיחוֹת הַתְּהִילּוֹת וְהַקִּינוֹת
בְּלִי רְשׁוּת בָּאנוּ לְפָנַיִךְ בְּחִיל וּרְעָדָה
שִׁלְחִי אֶת עֲווֹנֵנוּ עַל גַּב הַשָּׂעִיר
בִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ יָמוּת וַאֲנַחְנוּ נִתְאַבֵּל
כִּי חֲטָאֵינוּ כַּשָּׁנִים, הִלְבִּינָם כַּשֶּׁלֶג
The snare was broken and we escaped
The illusion was broken and we were the snare
Our hands were bloody not with our blood
Mother of mercy, and prayers of forgiveness, praise prayers, and lamentations
without permit we have come before you with fear and trembling.
Send our sins on the back of the goat
that it will die in our place and we will grieve
for our sins are as scarlet, make them white as snow.

This “Prayer for Yom Kippur” was shared by Rabbi Dr. Aryeh Cohen on 18 September 2026.
